name: Candle Cove
title: The Children's Show That Everyone Remembered Wrong
claims: Candle Cove is a creepypasta written by web cartoonist and author Kris Straub | 1
The story is framed as a discussion thread on the fictional NetNostalgia Forum | 1, 2
Users from the Huntington–Ashland area reminisce about Candle Cove | 1
Candle Cove was broadcast on Channel 58 in the early 1970s | 1
Another account places the show on a local channel in Ironton, Ohio in the 1970s | 2
The show centered on a young girl named Janice and imaginary adventures with marionette pirates | 1, 2
Creepy calliope music played over every episode | 2
Pirate Percy is a cowardly buccaneer who captains the Laughingstock, a living pirate ship with a wide mouth across its bow | 2
The Laughingstock repeatedly commands Percy "YOU HAVE… TO GO… INSIDE" | 2
Horace Horrible is one-eyed, with a handlebar mustache over too-tall teeth | 2
A skeleton in a tattered cape and top hat calls himself The Skin-Taker | 2
The Skin-Taker is described as a skeleton pirate wearing clothing made of children's skin | 1
An episode is recalled in which the characters just flail and scream | 1, 2
The story ends with a user relaying a conversation with his mother, who said the television showed only static when he claimed to be watching Candle Cove | 1
Rumors in the story say that when kids said they were watching it, parents saw only static | 2
Published in 2009 on Straub's website Ichor Falls under a Creative Commons license | 1, 2
Ichor Falls hosted horror stories about the fictional town of Ichor Falls | 1, 2
Straub was inspired by The Onion article "Area 36-Year-Old Still Has Occasional Lidsville Nightmare" | 1, 2
Lidsville was a 1970s children's television series | 1
One account dates the Onion article to 2000 | 2
Straub said the article was funny but the basic concept was frighteningly true | 2
Straub's quote about things that scare us as kids | 2
Straub said he wrote the story to get the idea out of his head | 2
These statements were made in a 2011 interview with Kindertrauma | 1, 2
Fans copied the story to larger horror sites without Straub's approval | 2
It was posted on creepypasta.com, the Creepypasta Wiki, 4chan, Reddit, YouTube, IGN, and horror.com | 1
Creepypasta is a neologism for horror stories circulated around the internet | 1
On some forums fans recreated the story's exchange as if it actually occurred | 1, 2
The story was often shared as some kind of urban legend and became somewhat detached from Straub | 2
A fan wiki has episode descriptions for two fan-invented seasons | 2
The wiki explores the 1767 book The Nickerbocker's Tale, supposedly inspiring the show, also a fan invention | 2
There is fan art, and videos and music, some claiming to be footage of the show | 2
Videos include people reading original creepypasta about seeing Candle Cove as children, and a mashup with Kids React | 2
Straub saw the growth as a flattering evolution and said not being litigious serves the mythos more | 2
Straub acknowledges his copyright and dislikes people making money from his work without authorization | 2
The Verge said most creepypasta have an anonymous folkloric quality while Candle Cove came from a known author | 1
Aeon called it among the best creepypastas and a good example of the forum format as storytelling | 1
The Verge called it a perfectly dark spin on nostalgia for half-remembered childhood stories | 1
A researcher attributed the popularity to verisimilitude and open-endedness, tied it to a Lovecraft renaissance, and described a terrible truth that cannot be unseen | 2
The researcher noted the barely explained show lets fans create their own versions | 2
Straub self-published Candle Cove and Other Stories in 2015 | 1
Syfy announced the adaptation in 2015 as the first season of Channel Zero | 1
The season centers on a child psychologist returning home to investigate 1980s disappearances | 1
Stars Paul Schneider and Fiona Shaw; premiered October 11, 2016 | 1
The show appears to credit Straub and includes a kid made of teeth | 2
Local 58 is an analog horror series spinoff of Candle Cove | 1
